stem: A Massachusetts health system is setting up collaborative drug therapy management across several of its sites. Which statements about who must approve it are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: In a licensed hospital, the Department of Public Health approves the arrangement.
A single system-wide approval suffices for every one of the listed settings.
In a long-term care facility, the facility's medical director or designee approves.
In a hospice setting, the hospice's medical director or designee approves.
An ambulatory care clinic additionally requires on-site physician supervision.

explanation.core_reasoning: The settings limb of the statute names a different approving body for each setting: the medical staff executive committee or designee in a licensed hospital, the medical director or designee in a long-term care facility, the hospice's medical director or designee in inpatient or outpatient hospice, and the clinic's medical staff executive committee or medical director or designee for an ambulatory care clinic, which uniquely also requires on-site supervision by the attending physician and a collaborating pharmacist.

choice_analysis.A: The statute names the medical staff executive committee or designee, not the Department.
choice_analysis.B: Each setting carries its own approval route.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the long-term care facility medical director.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: on-site supervision is unique to the ambulatory care clinic.

related_facts: Hospitals and ambulatory care clinics are both licensed under M.G.L. c. 111, s. 51
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates look for one governance route because the sites belong to one organisation.

reasoning_steps: Match it to the approving body the statute names
Note the extra on-site supervision condition for ambulatory care clinics
